documents.title: Hematology consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology and oncology group
Date of service: 01/16/2023
Referred for: macrocytic anemia

Ms. Duffy, 34, describes roughly six months of tiredness, recent intermittent palpitations, and a painful, raw tongue. She has ileocolonic Crohn's disease with a prior ileal resection, and she keeps a strict vegetarian diet. Her vitamin D deficiency has been treated and her PTH has normalized.

Current medications: albuterol as needed, prenatal multivitamin, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfonamides.

Exam: vital signs normal. Skin is pale. No jaundice, no lymphadenopathy, no splenomegaly. Neurologic screen without sensory loss.

Referring labs (12/06/2022): hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, MCV 105 fL.
Drawn here: homocysteine elevated, methylmalonic acid elevated.

Impression: Macrocytic anemia from vitamin B12 deficiency. The elevated MMA and homocysteine confirm a tissue-level deficiency. Loss of terminal ileum and a vegetarian diet both contribute.

Plan: start cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg by mouth daily, indefinitely. Repeat CBC in about 3 months through her PCP; we expect the hemoglobin and MCV to normalize. Please send her back if they do not.

Thank you.

documents.title: CBC on B12
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Karen - three months into B12 your hemoglobin is back to 12.3 and the red cell size is normal again (93). Nice response. Keep taking the B12 every day; it's long-term given your surgery. Fax copy to hematology.

documents.title: RE: CBC on B12
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great news. Tongue is totally back to normal and no more racing heart. Way more energy.

documents.title: Gastroenterology annual letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group
Visit: 05/09/2023

Annual Crohn's review. Ms. Duffy has had no flares; stools formed, no bleeding or pain. Since last year she was found to be deficient in vitamin D and B12, now replaced through endocrinology and hematology; this is consistent with her ileal resection and we will support ongoing supplementation.

Meds: albuterol prn, prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3 2000 units, B12 1000 mcg daily.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

Exam: abdomen soft, nontender.

Assessment: ileocolonic Crohn's disease, mild and inactive. No change; continue observation. Return in one year.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since around the new year, intercourse has become painful, and she gets spells of burning with urination every few weeks that settle on their own in a day or two. She also feels a sort of fullness or bulge at the front of the vagina. No fever, no flank pain, no discharge she's noticed. Has not had a UTI treated this year.

UA today: negative.

She preferred a gynecologist do the pelvic exam rather than me today.

A/P: dyspareunia, intermittent dysuria and anterior vaginal fullness, UA clean. Needs a pelvic exam by GYN. Referral placed. Return/call for fever or flank pain.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside women's health practice
Date of service: 07/17/2023

HPI: 34-year-old with Crohn's disease, recently treated vitamin D and B12 deficiency, and a long history of urinary tract infections, sent for six months of dyspareunia and on-and-off dysuria. She also notices a full feeling along the front wall of the vagina.

Allergies: penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).
Meds: albuterol prn, prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3, vitamin B12.

Pelvic exam: external genitalia normal. Speculum: cervix normal. On the anterior vaginal wall beneath the urethra there is a tender, soft mass; gentle pressure expresses a small amount of purulent fluid from the urethral meatus. Uterus and adnexa normal size, nontender.

Urinalysis in clinic: unremarkable.

Assessment: urethral diverticulum.

Plan: reviewed the diagnosis and its link to her infections and pain. Follow up here as needed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34F, annual. Feels the best she has in two years: energy back, no bone pain, tongue fine. Taking D3 2000 and B12 1000 daily without misses. Ferrous sulfate and prenatal vitamin also continuing.

Saw GYN in July - told she has a urethral diverticulum. Still some discomfort with sex, occasional burning, no fevers. GYN to follow as needed.
Crohn's quiet per GI in May. Asthma: one albuterol use this summer.

Exam: well. Vitals per flowsheet. Mucous membranes pink. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen nontender, port scars. No CVA tenderness. No edema. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Vitamin D deficiency / secondary HPT: on maintenance D3; check level and calcium.
2. B12 deficiency anemia: on oral B12; CBC and B12 level.
3. Urethral diverticulum: per GYN.
4. HM: Pap due - she asked to wait until after the GYN visit settled; will do with next physical. Flu/COVID next month at nurse visit.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything in range: vitamin D, B12, calcium, kidney and liver function, blood count. Continue the same supplements.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (L arm) and 2023-24 COVID (R arm) given. VIS provided. No prior vaccine reactions. Pt left after 15 min, feeling fine.

documents.title: Refill: albuterol
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx renewal request from pharmacy for albuterol HFA. Last filled 7 months ago. Approved per standing protocol, 1 inhaler + 3 refills. Pt notified via portal.

Outside gastroenterology group
Visit: 05/14/2024

Crohn's disease, ileocolonic, status post ileocecal resection 2020. Asymptomatic over the past year. Exam benign. Continues vitamin D and B12 replacement, and we agree with indefinite B12.

Allergies: penicillin, sulfonamides.

Plan: continue observation without maintenance medication. Yearly review.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology, satisfactory for evaluation, endocervical/transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.
reports.conclusion: NILM, HPV negative. Repeat co-testing in 5 years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35F. Doing well overall. Supplements daily. Diverticulum: intermittent discomfort and burning still, nothing that has sent her to urgent care this year; GYN has not needed to see her back. Crohn's stable, GI saw her in May. Asthma minimal.

Exam: well. BP/HR per flowsheet. Neck no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: external normal; speculum - cervix appears normal, co-test collected; mild tenderness anterior vaginal wall, known. No CVA tenderness.

A/P
1. HM: Pap/HPV done. PHQ-2 0. Flu shot next month.
2. Vitamin D / B12 deficiencies: labs today.
3. Urethral diverticulum, recurrent UTI hx: return early for fever, flank pain.
4. Crohn's, asthma: stable.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Karen - your Pap is normal and HPV negative, so you're set for 5 years. Vitamin D, B12, blood count and chemistries are normal. Have a good fall.

results.text: Greater than 100,000 CFU/mL Escherichia coli. Susceptible to ciprofloxacin.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital emergency department
Visit 11/11/2024

CC: fever, chills, left flank pain x3 days
HPI: 35F with Crohn's disease and a urethral diverticulum. A week of burning and frequency, then three days of fevers with shaking chills and pain in the left flank. No vomiting, tolerating fluids.
Allergies: penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).
Meds: albuterol prn, prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3, vitamin B12.

Triage: T 38.7 C, BP 110/68, HR 102, RR 18.
Exam: flushed, nontoxic. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Mild left CVA tenderness to percussion.

UA: pyuria with bacteriuria. Urine culture sent.

ED course: acetaminophen, 1 L normal saline, ceftriaxone 1 g IV given without reaction. Fever down, HR 88 at recheck. Tolerating PO.

Impression: acute pyelonephritis, left.
Disposition: home on ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. Follow up with PCP this week. Return for vomiting, worsening pain or persistent fever.

Addendum 11/13: urine culture >100K E. coli, susceptible to ciprofloxacin.

documents.title: Post-ED check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED record arrived. Pt on day 2 of cipro, fever broke yesterday, flank still sore but better. Eating and drinking. Culture grew E. coli sensitive to cipro - she's on the right drug. Appt with PCP 11/19. Reviewed when to go back to the ED.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED 11/11 for left pyelo, E. coli sensitive to cipro. Finished cipro yesterday. No fever since day 2, flank pain gone, no dysuria. First kidney infection of her life.

Exam: afebrile, looks well. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.
UA today negative.

A/P: left pyelonephritis, resolved. Diverticulum likely a reservoir. Reviewed hydration and early contact for symptoms; given her allergies, cipro worked well - note for next time.
